executiveSummary: This period saw multiple high-urgency incidents spanning financial fraud, election-targeted operations, and platform-level disruptions of state-linked influence. U.S. prosecutors charged suspects in a deepfake-enabled executive and attorney impersonation scheme that allegedly stole more than $129 million from companies across several countries, underscoring the scale and maturity of voice- and video-assisted social engineering against enterprise finance workflows Source View Article . UK authorities reported extensive AI-enabled investment endorsement scams abusing celebrity likenesses and trusted branding, with £24.3 million in reported losses across more than 1,300 cases Source . Election security remained a principal focus. Federal advisories warned that threat actors are using deepfake audio/video and AI-enhanced phishing against U.S. election and campaign officials, and urged verification steps including checking for content credentials or watermarking on suspicious media Security Advisory . Concurrent reporting documented likely foreign-linked election disinformation videos exploiting real people to target U.S. Senate races View Article , and China-linked "Spamouflage" personas posing as U.S. voters on social platforms Supporting Report . Across the platform and policy landscape, OpenAI reported disrupting Russian- and Iranian-linked false-front operations that used AI to fabricate personas, documents, and propaganda Source . Defensive and regulatory developments included EU guidance on machine-readable marking for AI-generated/manipulated content Guidance , continued newsroom and camera-maker progress on C2PA provenance, View Article and a NIST challenge supporting watermark benchmarking View Program . Meanwhile, new research demonstrated black-box evasion of commercial speech watermarks, signaling pressure on some provenance controls Supporting Report . Overall, the operational threat environment appears to be worsening given the volume and severity of high-urgency incidents in enterprise fraud, election interference, and consumer scams, alongside evidence of defense evasion targeting watermarking systems.

Enterprise finance controls: Require two-person verification and mandatory out-of-band callbacks (to known numbers) for urgent payment requests. Enforce cooling-off periods and segmented approval thresholds. (Analyst Recommendation)

Communications verification: Adopt shared passphrase or call-back channels for executive/legal communications; disable ad-hoc payment instructions over voice/video without secondary channel authentication. (Analyst Recommendation)

Identity and session hardening: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn); monitor for anomalous token use; apply conditional access on geo/behavior; rotate and revoke tokens rapidly after suspected compromise. (Analyst Recommendation)

Provenance workflows: Integrate C2PA/SynthID checks into newsroom and platform pipelines; preserve hashes and metadata; establish rapid provenance request paths with content originators. (Analyst Recommendation)

Election operations: Stand up a rapid-response "war room" for pre-bunking and counter-messaging; train staff on deepfake telltales; publish official channels and donation links prominently for verification. (Analyst Recommendation)

Law enforcement/public safety: Broadcast anti-impersonation guidance; publish callback numbers; coordinate with carriers on STIR/SHAKEN traceback; encourage citizens to end calls and re-dial official numbers. (Analyst Recommendation)
Legal readiness: Update incident playbooks for synthetic-media evidence handling; maintain chain-of-custody; retain forensic specialists for media authenticity analysis. (Analyst Recommendation)
